questions.prompt: You are writing an engineering application that rounds numbers to three or more decimal places. A function receives value, the number to format, and digits, the number of decimal digits to display. Which function returns the value with the specified number of decimal digits?
questions.explanation: The source answer is C. Number.prototype.toFixed receives the requested number of digits after the decimal point and returns a formatted string.
questions.answerLabel: C

questions.prompt: You are writing a script for Adventure Works. It must declare and initialize an array, fill it with ten random integers, and add every other number beginning with the first element. Complete the code.

pairs.left: [2] Add a number to the array

questions.explanation: The PDF selects [], push, j++, and array[j]. However, j = j++ assigns the old value back and fails to advance the loop; every-other-element traversal calls for j = j+2. The declared array is numbers, so the element expression should be numbers[j], not array[j]. The source key is retained but excluded from standard practice.
questions.answerLabel: See the source selections and matches below.

questions.prompt: You want to initialize a Date object for January 1, 2017 using numeric year, month, and day parameters. Select the year and month. The day value is fixed to 1 below from the explicit requirement; the PDF cuts off that part of the expression.
questions.exhibit: var date = new Date([1], [2], 1);
questions.explanation: The visible source selections are 2017 and 0. Numeric Date months are zero-based, so January is 0. The day argument 1 is supplied by the prompt’s January 1 requirement, rather than recovered from the clipped screenshot.
questions.answerLabel: See the source selections and matches below.

questions.prompt: Write a program that advises a person to ride a bike when the temperature is above 65 degrees and it is not raining. Otherwise, advise taking the train if the car has half a tank of gas or less, and driving the car when it has more fuel. Complete the source’s conditional structure.
questions.explanation: Use logical AND when both warm weather and the no-rain condition are required, and compare the fuel level with the stated threshold using <=.
questions.answerLabel: See the source selections and matches below.

questions.prompt: Create ticketPrice(age). Customers younger than 5 or at least 65 enter free. Customers aged 5 through 17 pay $10 USD; everyone else pays $20 USD. Complete the conditions.
questions.explanation: The free-admission ranges are alternatives, so join them with OR. A bounded youth range requires both its lower and upper bounds, so join those comparisons with AND.
questions.answerLabel: See the source selections and matches below.

questions.prompt: Write a JavaScript function that accepts a weekday string and returns the appropriate discount. Complete lines 03, 04, and 07 of the source function.
questions.explanation: A switch evaluates the day, the Wednesday case applies that discount, and default handles unmatched values. The break statements prevent unintended fall-through.
questions.answerLabel: See the source selections and matches below.

questions.prompt: Write a loop that traverses an array named list to find orange. If an element is null, immediately go to the next element. When orange is found, exit the loop. Complete the three keywords. The source clips the array literal and the right edge of the loop header; only those clipped portions are annotated below.
questions.explanation: A for loop traverses the array. continue skips the remainder of an iteration for a null value; break exits the loop after finding the target.
questions.answerLabel: See the source selections and matches below.

questions.prompt: Create a safe-division check with numerator and denominator parameters. It should return false when the denominator is zero and true otherwise. Review the code, then select Yes or No for each statement.

pairs.left: The function will always return false.
The operator at line 02 should be !=.

questions.explanation: The source marks No and No. Line 02 assigns 0 to denominator rather than comparing it; the assigned value is falsy, so this code takes the else branch. To meet the requirement, compare the denominator with zero (for example, denominator === 0), rather than replacing the operator with !=.
questions.answerLabel: See the source selections and matches below.

questions.prompt: Variable x has the value 5 and variable y has the value 7. Select True if each expression evaluates to true. Otherwise, select False.
questions.exhibit:
var x = 5;
var y = 7;
questions.explanation: Substitute x = 5 and y = 7 into each expression. The conjunction is true, the equality disjunction is false, x differs from 7, and negating x == y gives true.
questions.answerLabel: See the source selections and matches below.
